title: The First Forest

dek: Pristinia’s nearby woodland, crossed by working roads and dangerous expeditions. Its history includes a lost patrol, a town-shaped illusion and a quarry path reclaimed by growth.

body:
The First Forest begins close to Pristinia. Its roads and paths carry travelers toward Eovar, the Old Earth Hills and the quarry. The same woodland that shelters a road can conceal a ruined room, a missing patrol or an apparent way home that is not what it seems. These are connected parts of Prima’s landscape, with individual clearings and entrances still incompletely mapped.

Old growth and mist

The Eovar-road expedition of 2 May 2024 supplies an explicit route. The company leaves Pristinia, skirts parts of the First Forest and enters the Old Earth Hills. Pine, oak and birch tower above the road, with pockets of mist away from it. Farther on, the trees shorten and thin into scrub, and the road climbs through switchbacks.

This is an observed transition between named places. It does not make every cave reached from Pristinia part of the forest or fix the forest’s complete boundary. The route also explains why activity in the woods can affect travel and supplies well beyond the town.

11 April 2024 · the priest’s room

Elenia, Cobble, Talon, and Vigr Frami explored near the settlement and found an overgrown room containing the bones of a priest. The chamber supplied evidence of an older human presence but no living witness or convenient explanation. Its builder, faith, abandonment, and relationship to later events remain unresolved.

4 May 2024 · an ambush answers rescue

After a Pristinian patrol was ambushed in the First Forest, Symin answered the plea to find Tavorchanor and the missing group. He was killed near the ambush site, and bark-covered undead carried away his body. The loss made the forest’s proximity more dangerous rather than less: a threat did not need to cross a distant frontier to reach the settlement’s people.

Following voices into the blue mist

When Herb asks for help with the returning blue mist, Marius Antares recalls an earlier investigation deep in the First Forest. He and Heahmund Stormground leave Pristinia by the familiar forest road. The usual birds and insects fall silent; a rotten figure approaches and sings with voices the two men have reason to recognize.

Marius hears what seems to be his sister, while Heahmund hears his master. Those voices belong to the encounter’s lure. They do not establish that either person is physically standing in the forest. Blue mist thickens from a tree and makes the creature more dangerous. Marius notices a magical connection between them; weakening that connection and killing the attacker still leaves the mist behind.

Burning the tree does not destroy the sigil that sustains this part of the effect. Divine magic finally removes it, and this patch of mist lifts. The party goes on rather than treating one cleared patch as the end of the investigation.

The Pristinia they had not returned to

After more travel, the company appears to reach Pristinia’s gates. A supposed return to town becomes another fight: Herb seems to be attacked, villagers stare unnaturally, and the illusion gives way to more undead within the same mist. This is not evidence that the real town and its tavern have moved into the forest or that Herb dies there.

The mist restores fallen enemies. Marius detects another source in a ruined house, but when he tries to reach it Heahmund is overwhelmed. He turns back to help his companion recover, and they finish the fight. Kaelen joins them before they search the house. Destroying the second sigil with holy energy clears a larger area, and ghostly butterflies accompany their departure toward the real Pristinia.

The named forest, the outward road and the false town provide a strong route association. The exact clearing and the illusion’s full reach remain unrecovered; two destroyed sources do not establish permanent safety throughout every part of the woods.

A landscape that reclaims its routes

The quarry journey of 8 May 2026 takes another route through the First Forest. The narrator places it in the general direction of the Alpine Forest, then turns it off in the foothills. A path used only intermittently has been reclaimed by growth, and the party must find its way rather than follow a maintained road.

Camilla, Severina, Karnak and Selwyn reach a stone bridge over a frozen stream as the ground grows more mountainous. Wolves come out of the trees. After the fight, the surviving animals flee and the company continues for roughly another ninety minutes before reaching the snow-dusted quarry.

The forest approach, bridge and quarry are stages of the journey. The route does not place the quarry inside the Alpine Forest, and no surveyed connection to Kûn Ardaire or the harpy cave is supplied.

The open record

The First Forest’s complete boundaries remain unknown, as do the priest’s identity, the full reach of the bark-covered dead and the long-term condition of every area affected by blue mist. Its relationship to Al-Shomer cannot be settled by treating every underground entrance as the same place. The strongest recovered geography is the sequence of named roads, forest approaches and outward journeys.

The golden trail and Serath’s sacrifice

The narrator places the golden footprints in the First Forest. Serath, Thorn, Modeli, Dragos, Arethusa and Aleister follow them to the wounded Aionia through snow and failing magic. The encounter ends with Serath’s soul restoring the goddess and Modeli carrying her body toward Pristinia.

This gives the encounter a recovered setting rather than an unnamed refuge. It does not establish that every remote scene or change in the forest has the same cause. Read Serath’s sacrifice →
